mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and corporate earnings pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0 and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 6% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 140,000 new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140000 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS > 140000 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 1200 units for three consecutive months signals strengthening residential investment, which boosts construction sector earnings and overall economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1200 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when HOUST > 1200 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above 115 for three consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 115 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when INDPRO > 115 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
